package_info.package_name: MageCart web skimming script (injected via Picreel)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (JavaScript injected via third-party web marketing service)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (all sites integrating compromised Picreel code)
package_info.why_malicious: The MageCart script is malicious because it is injected into legitimate websites via a compromised third-party supplier (Picreel) and is designed to steal payment data from users by skimming sensitive information from web forms.

execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within the website's HTML (via Picreel's supplied code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the payment form's submit event, collects all form data (including payment details), and exfiltrates this data via an HTTP POST request to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in theft of sensitive user information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and sending data to an external, non-legitimate domain is a classic sign of web skimming and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal third-party marketing scripts should not access or transmit payment form data to unknown domains. Legitimate analytics or marketing scripts do not exfiltrate sensitive user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may transmit form data to their own secure endpoints, but only as part of authorized payment workflows and never to unrelated domains.
key_indicators: Collects all form data including payment details
Sends data to an external, non-affiliated domain
Injected via third-party supplier (supply chain attack)

attack_chain.action: MageCart group compromises Picreel, a third-party web marketing supplier.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is injected into Picreel's codebase.

attack_chain.action: Compromised Picreel code is loaded by Forbes and other client websites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious MageCart script executes in the context of the client websites.

attack_chain.action: MageCart script hooks into payment/subscription form submission events, collects sensitive data, and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment data from website users.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into form submission events
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests containing form or payment data to untrusted domains
Unexpected modification or injection of scripts from third-party suppliers
file_indicators: Injected or modified JavaScript in website HTML
References to external scripts from compromised third-party domains (e.g., Picreel)
Presence of event listeners on sensitive forms not present in original codebase
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to domains not associated with the website or its payment processor
Unusual traffic to newly registered or known MageCart infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to payment or subscription forms and sends form data to external domains. Inspect third-party scripts for unauthorized modifications. Use network monitoring to detect POST requests containing sensitive data to untrusted or known malicious domains. Employ file integrity monitoring on web assets to detect unauthorized script injections.
